A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SiD-LSG research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Revised and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Section 3 reports original SD1.5 and SD2.1-base distillation experiments, quantitative evaluations, and qualitative comparisons. The appendices include original computational measurements and FP16/FP32 analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative comparisons between selected SiD-LSG checkpoints in Figures 7–8.

M1.justification: The networks, alternating optimization, objectives, DDPM formulation, and guidance strategies remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 repairs generator sampling, noising, and guidance indices to agree with equations already present in v1; this does not establish a redesigned method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Aesthetics6+ training prompts, Aesthetics6.25+/6.5+ ablations, and COCO-2014 and HPSv2 evaluations. The new and revised qualitative examples remain within the existing text-to-image coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 6 retain their comparator membership. CogView2 gains an in-table citation, while DMD at CFG=3 remains a comparator despite removal of its CLIP value.

E3.justification: New Figures 7–8 compare five images per model for each of two shared prompts, using SD1.5 at guidance 1.5 and SD2.1-base at guidance 4.5. Figure 6 replaces one example prompt. The quantitative evaluation metrics, sample counts, and training settings remain unchanged; the new comparison does not isolate guidance from backbone differences.

E4.justification: Figures 7–8 add case studies examining diversity, text alignment, and visual quality across two selected checkpoints. Existing guidance, training-duration, batch-size, prompt-selection, and precision analyses remain, including the FP16/FP32 analysis renumbered from Figure 7 to Figure 9.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same random-seed matching statement for qualitative comparisons. Neither adds repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces DMD (CFG=3)'s CLIP value of 0.32 with a dash; its FID remains 11.49. SiD-LSG's quantitative scores and ablation curves are retained. New Figures 7–8 add qualitative results, Figure 6 replaces the puppy-at-a-window row with a dog-watching-television row, and the example galleries are refreshed.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the noise-prediction loss expression by assigning kappa2 to the fake network and kappa4 to the teacher, restoring agreement with its denoising expression. Its generator noising expression also restores a_t. The underlying score identities, MESM derivation, and assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim data-free one-step Stable Diffusion distillation through long-short guidance, without additional regression or adversarial losses. The headline COCO-2014 FID of 8.15 with CLIP 0.304 and the scope of the claimed contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 and Figures 7–8 add a perceptual interpretation: the selected low-FID model produces greater diversity, while the selected high-CLIP model better follows text and has stronger aesthetic quality. This expands the existing numerical tradeoff discussion, although the illustrated models also differ in backbone. Appendix D's limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The abstract and conclusion change a promised code/model release into a statement of public availability. Appendix E expands several recorded prompts with style and control suffixes, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Documentation remains imperfect: it retains the old puppy prompt after Figure 6 replaces that example.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds an explicit comparison with earlier methods, distinguishing SiD-LSG through score-network backpropagation, placement of guidance, and its Fisher-divergence objective. This clarifies positioning relative to SwiftBrush and other distillation approaches; the bibliography itself is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the guidance explanations and conclusion, revises release wording in the abstract, and adds qualitative interpretation and a related-work comparison paragraph. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 7–8, revises Figure 6 and the example galleries, and enlarges gallery prompt labels. Former Figures 7–8 become Figures 9–10, while quantitative display structures largely persist. A new layout defect makes Table 3's caption overlap its column header.

improvement.justification: Correcting Algorithm 1 reduces implementation ambiguity, while the reported code/model release and clearer research positioning improve reproducibility documentation and explanation. These gains are limited: the quantitative evidence is essentially unchanged, the new visual comparisons vary both backbone and guidance, Appendix E retains an outdated Figure 6 prompt, and Table 3 introduces a caption overlap.
